method: Inputs: the eight extraction files of the 25 sources (314 recommendations, 213 rejected ideas, 146 open questions, 168 cut / merge candidates, 111 findings without a recommendation) and the completeness critic's duplicates, conflicts and gaps. Merging: recommendations that describe the same change become one finding that keeps every source id; the critic's owner note supplies the design. A recommendation that bundles separable work is split: its id sits in the sources of the finding that carries its main part, and the other finding says 'Split:' in its notes. Every source id therefore appears exactly once, in a finding's sources or in not_adopted. Sources that are not recommendation ids (a finding without a recommendation, a critic gap) are marked as such. Floor: read strictly; where its text does not clearly permit something it is treated as outside, and where two files disagree the stricter reading is the resolution unless a ruling says otherwise. Settled decisions stand: a part that needs to change one whose Reverses-if is not met is not adopted, or becomes a question when the operator's explicit wants depend on it; amendment lines that only add detail are recorded with the landing commit. Tiers: P0 = confirmed defects that leak, lose or corrupt data or weaken a floor guarantee, plus the go-public blockers B1-B7 and what else must hold before the first public push; P1 = the operator's explicit wants (no-scroll Play, few tabs, zero-click, the build and item pains, go-public, deployable like the reference app, no-reminder automation) and what unblocks them; P2 = high player value and hardening; P3 = worthwhile; P4 = defer. Rank inside a tier: findings that can start (plan, needs-ruling, operator) before blocked ones, deferred last; then score = impact (H 3, M 2, L 1) divided by effort (S 1, M 2, L 3) plus 0.5 per finding that directly depends on it (at most 3; the three findings that gate all parallel work get the full 3); a finding never ranks before a same-tier finding it depends on; ties keep the order of the operator's want list. Rank numbers run through the tiers, so rank 1 is the first P0 finding. Dispositions: plan (a session or wave can do it now), blocked (the exact condition is stated), needs-ruling (question ids of the Open decisions section), operator (the act), defer (why). Field text (risk, ToS check, acceptance, ZERO-CLICK, files) comes from the owning source unless the merge changed it; R-, F- and B-numbers inside such text are that source's own. Rulings: all 28 questions were ruled by adjudicator agents on 2026-11-18 (section Rulings); each finding carries its ruled disposition, a finding ruled out or outside the current floor text moved to not_adopted with the ruling as its reason, and the items only the operator can decide are listed under Operator decisions with the default the plan follows meanwhile. Floor audit: three independent auditors, each told to refute compliance, checked every finding and ruling against the floor on 2026-11-18 (section Floor audit). An id flagged by two or three lenses took the strictest fix; an id flagged by one lens took the stricter reading too unless the flag was plainly mistaken; no doubt was resolved in favour of the looser reading. A flagged finding was reworked to its floor-safe form or blocked on an operator decision; no source id moved, so coverage is unchanged.
summary: 1. Three confirmed defects are documented in tracked research and must be fixed before anything is public: the token-free /web/ route resolves UNC paths (F-002), a build payload with a NUL byte passes the DTD guard (F-005), and a core with a missing log path tails the live Client.txt outside the opt-in indicator (F-001). F-006 ties the visibility flip to them.
2. Two data-integrity defects sit beside them: runtime files are written without fsync, retry or backup (F-014) and a log break can replay a backlog into thousands of false deaths (F-015).
3. History has not been scanned for the names of the reviewed third-party set (F-004); it is the one go-public unknown.
4. Nothing in the plan runs in parallel safely until the ledger rule (F-017), the loop parser fix (F-024) and safe overlapping tests (F-022) land; HALT comes off only after six checks (F-078).
5. No-scroll Play is measured and fits with every sibling change applied: build F-025, put the budgets under test (F-066), adopt one type scale (F-053) and four tabs (F-067).

6. The build pain has one floor-safe fix ruled in, the hotkey load (F-042; Q-02); the save-file pick (F-058) waits for one read-list line from the operator, and reading Path of Building's builds folder is outside the current floor text and not adopted unless the operator amends the read list (Q-01); a current-shape character paste loses every mod today (F-035).
7. The item pain: a staged verdict that answers at once (F-059), a keep-or-vendor verdict with no build (F-060), a worn-gear baseline (F-070) and an honest caveat on every verdict (F-043).
8. Prices are silently blocked today without a typed contact (F-018) and refresh only while the page is open (F-036); league identity must be ready before 2026-12-11 (F-031).

9. Go-public is about two days of agent work plus the operator's go: guarded push and rules (F-016), CI (F-013), fresh-clone proof (F-008), then F-021; a stranger's source install is broken until F-019.

10. Deployment like the reference app is one design now (per-user home, version folders, pinned runtimes, install line, Apps & features entry, staged updates): F-038 first, then F-049, F-047, F-048, F-050, F-063, F-077.

11. No-reminder automation: one watcher frame (F-030), rows filed as add-only files (F-029), a launch gate that opens the 1.0 rows by itself before 2026-12-10 (F-052); new sources follow the dev host's web-data switch and read repository metadata only; policy quotes under watch (F-051) wait for the operator's floor line on GGG's docs pages (A-01).

12. The open live checks close without scheduled operator sessions: log shapes by a consented parse ledger (F-061), RAM and CPU by AshLight's own budget log (F-032), in-game tries by one click each (F-062).
13. Reliability and observability follow as P2: the client survives its own errors, nothing stays down, every log is bounded, Checks explains causes.
14. Dated items: tree hold by 2026-12-08, launch gate by 2026-12-10, league identity by 2026-12-11, Electron 45 line ends about 2027-04-27, GGG registration expected to reopen about 2027-01.

15. The operator is asked once (docs/plan/09): the eleven operator decisions below, a handful of one-minute acts and four in-game tries (F-040); every item carries a default the plan follows meanwhile.

16. Blocked on others: GGG OAuth registration and GGG's written answers on token storage and log-triggered reads (F-080, F-116, F-149), poe.ninja's answer before any release build polls it (F-046), and an outbound note path to the fleet owner (F-203).

17. Floor audit: three independent auditors checked all 211 findings and 28 rulings; 28 ids were flagged and every one took the stricter reading (24 reworked to a floor-safe form, 4 blocked on the operator, none rejected, none kept as it was). Two conflicts between the strict reading and settled behaviour go to the operator: the docs watch pages (A-01) and the Steam library scan (A-03).

Floor audit (L3): a wider discovery scan before the opt-in is a read the floor list does not name, so this finding adds none; whether today's Steam library scan (Steam's registry key and libraryfolders.vdf, server/al/logfile.py) is on the read list is operator decision A-03.

findings.title: Four in-game tries by the operator
findings.action: The operator (1) loads one AshLight-made .build in game, (2) pastes one search string to confirm a leading '!' negates the whole OR group, (3) imports the downloaded filter snippet, (4) loads a merged real filter; each ends in one click on the 'Tried in game' card.
findings.risk: Low.

findings.zero_click: Each try ends in one click; no typed report.
findings.disposition: operator: four in-game tries, one click each (one batched ask)

findings.title: REL-NOTES: one changelog generator

findings.zero_click: Prepared unattended; one operator phrase per release.

findings.title: Memoise the static floor scan; small timer fixes
findings.action: tests/test_floor_static.py caches per-file regex hits keyed by (path, size, mtime_ns); shorten the keepalive e2e constants and two 0.5 s polls; AL_FUZZ_S=0.1 in per-package checks only; drop the pid literal.

findings.tos_check: File is the floor's static guard; all 29 plants, 3 mutation tests and live-tree scan stay; nothing skipped.

findings.zero_click: Runs in the suite.

findings.title: CLIENT-GUARD and OBS-CRASH: the client survives its own errors without a dialog, and every exit leaves a record
findings.action: app/main.js: uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers that log the stack and carry on (3 in 60 s: relaunch); render-process-gone, unresponsive and did-fail-load handlers rebuild the overlay at most 3 times in 10 minutes and reload the companion; the core writes ops/runtime/last-exit.json on every exit path; Checks reads both.
findings.risk: A handler can hide a real bug; every event logged with stack, caps stop a loop.
findings.tos_check: Handlers run only on failure events in main process; page gets no timer; overlay rule kept.
findings.acceptance: Node tests: an error thrown in the main process logs its stack and opens no dialog; three errors in 60 s relaunch once; a killed overlay renderer is rebuilt at most 3 times in 10 minutes; last-exit.json is written on stop, reload, signal and crash; the overlay budget test stays green.
findings.zero_click: Automatic; tray tooltip changes only after the cap.
findings.notes: No error box can take focus from the game. The core never restarts the client (decision 0041 point 2); the client relaunches itself.

findings.title: OBS-SSE-EVENTS: stop sending chat-bearing frames by default
findings.action: Stop sending the 'events' SSE frame by default; keep it as a dev tap (/events?tap=1, source checkout only) with text fields removed; drop the unused recent_whispers field from the snapshot; move the 4 tests that read the frame to the tap.
findings.risk: A hidden consumer; grep shows none in web/ or app/.
findings.tos_check: Reduces what is passed on; reads nothing new.
findings.acceptance: Default stream holds 0 'events' frames over a fixture replay and state pushes still arrive within 250 ms.
findings.zero_click: Nothing to do.
findings.notes: Also carries the cut of recent_whispers (0038 cut list: unused and carries chat text).

findings.title: CALC-PRIORITY: heavy child processes below normal priority
findings.action: Start luajit and every batch child AshLight runs (code preflight, drift trial, snapshot build) with the below-normal priority class; core and client stay at normal.
findings.risk: A press takes longer on a saturated CPU; with R3 the first card does not depend on it.
findings.tos_check: 'Never touches the game process': only AshLight's own child processes get a creation flag.
findings.acceptance: A test reads the priority class of the started luajit and the preflight child and expects below normal.
findings.zero_click: Automatic.

findings.title: BUDGET-TESTS: enforce the measured budgets
findings.action: test_budgets.py runs the real loop body 10 s on the worst-case fixture and checks absolute working set in a child; new deterministic tests for tick cost, idle tick, start parse count and snapshot size; a CDP dashboard perf test; the calc ceilings of decision 0024 R7 at about 2.5 times today's values.
findings.risk: Timing flakes; prefer deterministic checks, keep fleet_test_guard.budget on timed ones.
findings.tos_check: Tests only; live smoke shows AshLight's own window and stays opt-in.
findings.acceptance: Each new test fails with its defect put back once and passes without it.
findings.zero_click: The suite runs them.
findings.notes: Budgets B1-B19 of note 0048 are adopted as the numbers. The live smoke stays opt-in.

findings.title: OBS-REPORT: the report built from structured fields
findings.action: GET /api/report builds the report on click from an allow-list of structured fields (build, OS build, Python / Electron versions, Checks rows, counters, last exit and restarts, ledger shapes when on); read-only preview before copy; no log tails by default, an explicit second choice adds them through a hardened redactor.
findings.risk: Copy must stay inside the click's activation; test in client window and a browser.
findings.tos_check: No upload (ruling J); clipboard written only on the player's click (0014); nothing new read.
findings.acceptance: Fuzz test with L3 strings and 1,000 seeded variants finds no seeded secret in output; snapshot holds no report text and its version stays still over 3 idle minutes with web data on and last line 5 min old; preview equals copied text byte for byte.
findings.zero_click: One click to copy (0014 requires it); preview costs no extra click.
findings.notes: No upload, ever; the clipboard is written only on the player's click. Carries AUDIT-P8-LOW P8-7 (redact must not blank fixed report words).

findings.title: One hardening pass over the Electron shell
findings.action: New app/guards.js before any window: app.enableSandbox(); a web-contents-created default that denies navigation, popups and webview attach unless the creator registered a policy; webgl off; quit on an inspect switch, a remote-debugging port or NODE_OPTIONS without AL_DEV=1; run.ps1 drops ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE and NODE_OPTIONS from the client environment; one contract test with a single ban list.

findings.tos_check: Overlay rule: no new process, timer or window, budgets hold; no input; launcher still starts only repo scripts.
findings.acceptance: With fake webContents an unregistered one has navigation, popups and webview attach refused; both origin spellings granted and a foreign file URL ending /overlay/index.html gets empty reply; fake spawn receives absolute paths; live smoke still shows 2 processes under 215 MB.
findings.zero_click: Nothing for the player.

findings.title: An egress lock on both Electron sessions
findings.action: webRequest.onBeforeRequest on the default session and the client partition cancels every request that is not an app file page, the loopback core on the configured port, or devtools with AL_DEV=1; the icon render page gets a no-network CSP.
findings.risk: Blob and data URLs must pass; one callback per request.
findings.tos_check: Enforces 'trade site never called by the app' and web-data-off rule inside Electron.
findings.acceptance: Unit test of the allow function over 20 URLs; opt-in smoke with an external image logs one cancelled request.
findings.zero_click: Nothing for the player.
findings.notes: A second guard for two floor rules inside the client: the trade site is never called by the app, and nothing hits the network while web data is off.

findings.title: Narrow external links and downloads
findings.action: Open a link only while the companion has focus, at most 1 per second and 5 per minute, https only, with the parsed href, hosts from one tracked list shared with web/tc.js; accept downloads only from the core origin with extension .build, .filter, .json or .txt; log each refusal.
findings.risk: A new link host must join the list; a test enumerates what web/ emits.
findings.tos_check: Keeps decision 0017 (user opens trade URL in own browser); click stays the player's.
findings.acceptance: routeFor denies without focus, on the sixth link in a minute and for http; a download named x.exe is cancelled.
findings.zero_click: Link click is the player's own act; no new prompt.

findings.title: UTIL-ASC-FROM-TREE: ascendancy names from the cached tree
findings.action: Read the class to ascendancy map from the cached GGG tree export (Data Exports) first and keep the built-in table as fallback; a name enters the built-in table only when it is in the cached tree export or in operator-pasted patch text (the 3 missing names now, the 1.0 names when GGG publishes the export).
findings.risk: Low.
findings.tos_check: Names from GGG's published tree export (Data Exports) read from the local cache, or from operator-pasted text; no forum, wiki or poe2db read (Q-07; floor audit L1, L3); nothing new bundled.
findings.acceptance: With a synthetic tree naming a new ascendancy, class_fits knows its class with no code change; each name added to the built-in table is present in the cached tree export fixture or in a pasted-text record cited by the commit.
findings.zero_click: Follows the tree file.
findings.notes: 1.0 names (0038 F13) are re-checked at launch (F-052) against the cached tree export and operator-pasted patch text only; no agent reads the patch notes. Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked (tree export and pasted text are the only name sources).

findings.title: DIAG-DATA-AGE: say when the game data is older than the game
findings.action: When the log names a campaign or map area id the cached world_areas file lacks, show a Checks row 'Game data is older than your game' with the fix step.

findings.title: Give the GGG docs watch a 'shape' topic
findings.action: A topic keyed on the field names the reader uses, so a diff of the API Reference page (/developer/docs/reference) or the Data Exports page (/developer/docs/data) touching them is tagged and the note line names the fields. The topic does not run on the changelog or the other docs pages unless the operator's floor line (A-01) allows them (one constant, off).
findings.risk: None; dev tool, read only.
findings.tos_check: GGG pages inside the floor's two named sets only (API Reference, Data Exports), at the cadence of decision 0044; no API call. Floor audit (L1): the other four docs pages are outside both sets under Q-07's reading, so the topic leaves them out.
findings.acceptance: A synthetic reference diff that retypes explicitMods gets topic 'shape' and a note naming the field; a synthetic changelog diff gets no 'shape' tag while the A-01 constant is off.
findings.zero_click: Runs on the loop tick, also while HALTed.
findings.notes: Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked to the reference and data pages.

findings.title: Build the offline core of a GGG client
findings.action: In a module outside providers.py with an injected transport: the OAuth User-Agent form, PKCE and state, authorize URL, token exchange, the header-driven limiter, a one-shot 127.0.0.1 listener (state and path checked, closes after one request); the access token is held in memory only; refresh (7-day ceiling) and the OS credential store sit behind one constant that is off by default and is turned on only by a decision citing GGG's written reply to the F-083 refresh question; the bearer token never follows a redirect.
findings.risk: Rests on details only GGG's reply settles (port matching, refresh on/off); a declined application wastes the day.
findings.tos_check: No request possible without a client id; later requests only to API Reference hosts, GGG UA form, headers obeyed dynamically, no POESESSID; listener binds 127.0.0.1 on a block port. Floor audit (L2): GGG's docs say refresh tokens must be stored securely on a server, so nothing keeps a token on the player's PC until GGG allows it in writing.
findings.acceptance: D-AUTH's verifier/challenge example round-trips; with the constant off no refresh request is built and no credential-store call is made (transport and store injected, 0 calls); with it on in a test a refresh never moves the stored ceiling; limiter honours synthetic headers and Retry-After; listener refuses wrong state, path or Host; no token in state snapshot, log, diag report or settings export.
findings.zero_click: Not applicable until wired (R5).
findings.notes: No request is possible without a client id; details that depend on GGG's reply stay behind constants. Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked (refresh and stored tokens behind a default-off constant).

findings.title: Recover a refused share link in one click
findings.action: On the web-data-off refusal the status line offers 'Turn on web data and load this link'; the click shows the same opt-in sentence as the Settings card (everything web data turns on) and only a confirm click on that sentence saves the opt-in and repeats the load.
findings.risk: A privacy switch behind a button; the label must name it.
findings.tos_check: The confirm click on the full opt-in sentence is the explicit opt-in of 0013; floor audit (L3): a label naming only the link would turn on more than the player saw. Fetch stays one request to an allow-listed host with truthful UA; nothing without the confirm.
findings.acceptance: Node test: the refusal renders the button; the first click posts nothing and shows the opt-in sentence (one string shared with Settings); the confirm click posts the opt-in, then the same code once.
findings.zero_click: Two clicks replace four acts.
findings.notes: The confirm click is the explicit opt-in of decision 0013; web data is never turned on without it. Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked (the full opt-in sentence is shown before anything is saved).

findings.title: Overlay parts chooser, a sample card, and a quiet overlay
findings.action: Settings group 'Overlay shows' with switches per part and two presets (Full, Cards only), plus 'Show a sample card for 10 s'; the HUD card hides entirely when no part has content; 'hide in town and hideout' for the zone line; in_hideout is decided from the area id of the generation line, not an English scene-name substring.

findings.action: The one card slot also shows a zone card for 12 s on first entry of a campaign zone with a goal and an act card for 12 s when an act split closes; slot order: open trade card, item / price / waystone card, zone or act card, first-run key hint, nothing.

Settles S5 (a), the UX-ZONE-NOTES overlay word and UTIL-OVERLAY-MAP. On by default with a switch in the parts chooser. Design 0001 section 10 amendment through the design reviewer.

findings.action: When an incoming trade whisper has the same sender and item text as an open card, update that card's time and price fields instead of appending; recent whispers still log every line.
findings.risk: L: two genuine requests for identical items from one buyer merge; whisper log still shows both.

findings.acceptance: Three identical whispers from one sender and one from another: trade_requests has 2 rows, the first with the newest 'at'; 'Trade accepted.' still closes one card.
findings.zero_click: Automatic.

findings.title: An in-browser accessibility pass in the CDP harness
findings.action: Extend app/test/cdp with an a11y job over one fixture state: AX tree (no unnamed focusable, no skipped heading level, landmark set), a real Tab walk on every tab with ring visibility per stop, forced-colours emulation, 320 CSS px reflow and the four text-spacing overrides, in dark and light with folds open.
findings.risk: Low; headless Chrome already a test dependency; must skip cleanly where Chrome is absent.
findings.tos_check: Drives AshLight's own page in windowless Chrome with synthetic Tab keys to that page only; nothing reaches the game, no clipboard or screen read.
findings.acceptance: New pytest runs ~10 s, fails on a planted clipped ring, planted unnamed button and planted 3:1 pair; green on main after R2 and R3.
findings.zero_click: A test; no player step.
findings.notes: Closes the research gap that the WCAG verdict rests on Play only. Drives AshLight's own page in a windowless browser.

findings.title: One guide file, ready for 1.0
findings.action: Fold zone_notes.json and the boss table into zone_guide.json (goal, bonus, layout, next, boss element) and print one guide block; fill the 4 blank zones and check the '+2 point books' wording only from the allowed fact sources: the attributed build-time snapshots (credited in theorycraft/datacredit.py), GGG Data Exports, AshLight's own Client.txt observations (the F-061 ledger, the operator's own play) and operator-pasted text; a fact that would need a live wiki, poe2db or GGG forum read is left out; one level-gap rule (zoneguide.advice reads underlevel_gap). At launch: drop interlude acts once live ids confirm it and write Acts 5-6 entries from the same sources, best effort, with no deadline.
findings.risk: Thin sources at launch; ship goals first, leave unsure facts out (decision 0043 rule); Acts 5-6 may stay sparse for days. Merge is S; 24 zones of own-word notes is the rest.
findings.tos_check: Floor audit (L1, L3): poe2db / wiki data only as attributed build-time snapshots after a licence check, and no GGG forum read (Q-07); so guide facts come only from the snapshots (under the web-data opt-in), GGG Data Exports, AshLight's own Client.txt observations and operator-pasted text, restated in own words (decisions 0009, 0043). No agent or tool reads a live wiki, poe2db or forum page for the guide.
findings.acceptance: One data file; every campaign area id in the cached snapshot has a goal or explicit skip; zone tile shows no separate 'Zone tip'; boss hint fires for every zone with a boss element; after launch G5 and G6 ids covered or explicitly skipped; every new or changed entry carries src and checked (F-097) naming one of the four allowed sources; a test refuses a wiki, poe2db or GGG forum host in any src field.
findings.zero_click: Data only; file hot-reloads (decision 0042).
findings.notes: Split: S5 (a) is F-119, (b) was F-211, not adopted (Q-26 (b): the upgrade list stays memory-only), (d) (clear-or-push threshold) is tuned from two weeks of F-061 data, (e) is F-050. The launch part is gated by F-052. Facts restated in own words, unsure facts left out. Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked (fact sources named, the 48-hour launch clock dropped).

findings.title: Upgrade search per slot from the build
findings.action: Put the trade-search link (same builder) on every 'Look for next' row so a search for any slot needs no item press first.
findings.risk: The ?q= link form is undocumented (decision 0017 clause).
findings.tos_check: Pasted build and cached stat-id snapshot; decision 0017 (URL opened in player's browser; no trade endpoint call); ids per decision 0037.

findings.action: Every source records last_ok; 3 failures in a row add one tick line; 7 days of failure file WATCH-BROKEN-<NAME>; a halted tick writes pending findings into its checklist; the dev-host Checks view notes a last tick older than 2 h.
findings.risk: None.

findings.acceptance: Source failing since 8 days yields one row, once.

findings.title: A four-page player guide
findings.action: Download, Quick start, Common issues and FAQ pages built from the footer promise list and the Checks fix lines; the FAQ answers 'Is it allowed? Can I be banned?' first and honestly; README and About name the one download place.
findings.risk: Wording that sounds like an endorsement.

findings.title: SECOND-LINE: nothing stays down
findings.action: run.ps1 starts the supervisor before waiting for health and hands it the core pid (--adopt-pid, 60 s grace); the core starts a missing supervisor (at most once per 5 min, never against stop.request); the client checks /api/health every 30 s and after 4 failures runs run.ps1 once, at most once per 15 min.
findings.risk: Restart loops; every layer keeps its cap and stop.request wins.
findings.tos_check: Only AshLight's own python processes, proven by pid and creation time (decision 0010); game never listed (0029); 0041 stands: supervisor never starts Electron.
findings.zero_click: Automatic; 'Keepalive was not running; AshLight started it again.' on Checks card.
findings.notes: Recorded as a decision 0005 amendment at landing (adds neighbours, reverses nothing). No new watchdog process.

findings.title: OVL-CHECK: the in-map overlay check as one normally played map
findings.action: Developer-only tools/ovl_check.py armed by a session: starts 20 s into an open map, cycles the overlay through nine 30 s blocks (hidden, shown, updating) with own-window calls only, records AshLight's own processes and system-wide totals each second, and asks the operator once at the end whether the game's own FPS display stayed the same or dropped; JSON and a 15-line summary in <sidecar>\Logs. No screen capture; the phase switch stays in tools/ and drives the overlay through its existing calls (Q-18).
findings.risk: The HUD blinks for 4.5 min of one map; the result is a proxy, blind at a saturated GPU or an FPS cap; the display mode is not detected.

Enforced by the allow-list in code and the spawn arguments, not by prompt wording; no forum or trade URL anywhere.
findings.acceptance: The allow-list function refuses a GGG forum URL, a trade URL, a /developer/docs/changelog URL (A-01 off), a poe2db URL and a wiki URL, and passes the reference and data pages; a dive spawn carries no WebFetch or WebSearch tool (test on the spawn arguments); every fetch of a fixture dive is in the host log with the AshLight User-Agent; a request with open rows present still dispatches one dive; a request carrying a refused URL dispatches nothing; a test finds no forum host in the dive prompt or the runbook.

findings.title: One real screen-reader pass
findings.action: After the accessibility fixes land, an agent runs a screen reader over the dashboard on a fixture core and records what is heard for page load, an item check, a trade request, a tab switch and the Settings form. Keys go to the page through the browser driver, never the OS input queue; the transcript is the reader's own speech log, with no screen or audio capture.
findings.risk: Needs a visible window and audio on the operator's machine, so must run when the operator is not playing.
findings.tos_check: Reads AshLight's own page with an OS reader. Floor audit (L3): the floor bars any input to the game and any screen read outside a manual press, so the pass runs only with the game closed (the operator's word and game_idle true from Client.txt staleness), sends no OS-level key event and captures no screen or audio.
findings.acceptance: A dated transcript from the reader's speech log per step, no unnamed or doubled announcements; the run script refuses to start unless game_idle is true and the operator flag is given, and contains no OS input or capture call.
findings.zero_click: A dev task; no player step.
findings.disposition: blocked: the operator confirms the game is closed (not only that they are not playing) and game_idle is true; speech output and a visible browser on this machine
findings.notes: Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked (game closed, driver keys only, speech log only).

findings.risk: Low.
findings.tos_check: No floor rule; the CLAUDE.md bind rule (127.0.0.1 only, LAN access off) stands (Q-11 ruled P0); only an operator pick of design C would lift or scope it.
findings.acceptance: Nothing changes in the tree; a later pick of P1, B or C is recorded in a decision before any work, and C also lifts or scopes the bind rule and amends the decision 0002 token wording.
findings.zero_click: Nothing by default.

findings.title: Peek key for one-screen players
findings.action: An optional third AshLight key shows a compact detail in the existing overlay card slot (click-through, non-focusable, one card at a time per decision 0014) and hides it on the next press. AshLight never shows the companion window on the game's monitor; the companion opens only on another display (F-167).
findings.risk: The one card slot is small (design section 10); a third global key; the overlay budgets (decision 0002) must hold with the detail card.
findings.tos_check: Floor audit (L1): the overlay must be a separate transparent, always-on-top, click-through, non-focusable window; a focusable companion placed over the game would act as a second overlay without those properties and could take focus from the game. So the detail is drawn inside the existing overlay window; the press reads and sends nothing; nothing queries or activates the game window (decision 0029 amendment).
findings.acceptance: Node test: one press shows the detail card in the overlay slot, the next hides it, a held key does not repeat; the overlay window stays non-focusable and click-through while the card shows (flags asserted); the handler makes no clipboard or screen call and no show or focus call on the companion window; unset by default; tests/test_budgets.py green.
findings.zero_click: Off by default; one press when the player wants detail.
findings.disposition: defer: needs an operator taste call; no demand evidence; the detail must fit the one overlay card slot

findings.title: Spike: one press per item by a screen read
findings.action: Time-boxed test: one capture of the tooltip area on the AshLight spike-key press, read by the OS engine (an external OCR tool only after a decision pins it by hash with a licence check), compared offline against the clipboard text of the same 30 items taken by separate item-key presses or from fixtures. Each manual press does exactly one read, the screen or the clipboard, never both. The image is discarded after the read, never stored and never sent off the PC.
findings.risk: Misread numbers give wrong verdicts; an external OCR tool needs its own decision and pin (core stays stdlib-only, 0002); OS engine languages depend on device install (English recognizer presence UNVERIFIED).
findings.tos_check: One read per manual AshLight key press is what the floor and GGG allow; floor audit (L2, L3): a press that read both the screen and the clipboard would be two reads, and no unpinned external tool may see a game image. No continuous capture, timer or input; capture by AshLight's own window process, not a hook in game graphics.
findings.acceptance: A test proves the spike-key handler makes exactly one screen read and 0 clipboard reads and the item-key handler one clipboard read and 0 screen reads; no image file is written; 30 of 30 items parse to the same stats as their clipboard text, or the spike is closed as rejected.
findings.zero_click: 1 press, floor minimum for any item read.
findings.disposition: defer: after the changed item key the saving is one key press per item; no wave before 1.0; a pick-one-of-N recommender (0056-Q2) waits with it and would need one manual press per screen read
findings.notes: Floor audit 2026-11-18: reworked (one read per press, OS engine only, image never stored).

findings.title: CLOCK-STEP: timers survive a clock change
findings.action: The core loop compares wall and monotonic deltas each pass; a difference over 5 s shifts the stored stamps by the step under the state lock.
findings.risk: Many stamps; one SessionState method, property test.
findings.tos_check: No floor rule touched.
findings.acceptance: Fixed-clock test: a +3600 s step leaves zone time, act splits and idle state unchanged.
findings.zero_click: Automatic.
findings.disposition: defer: low impact; last reliability wave

open_decisions.question: May AshLight read files Path of Building writes on the player's disk: the builds folder (opt-in, path shown, newest fitting file per loop tick) or PoB's local API answer file? The floor's READ ONLY list names only Client.txt, the per-press clipboard / screen read and public web data.
options: no: the list is exhaustive; the hotkey load and the file pick carry the build pain
yes for the builds folder: opt-in under a new decision and one added line in the CLAUDE.md read list
yes for the folder and the API answer file
open_decisions.recommendation: No until the operator rules in their own words. They are not game files and GGG's rules do not speak of them, but the list as written is exhaustive and no adjudicator can widen the floor; the strict reading wins. The plan builds the hotkey load and the file pick first; a yes later adds the folder source on top with no rework.

open_decisions.question: Decision 0004 speaks of user-pasted build text. Does a build loaded by the item-check hotkey press (the same single clipboard read) or from a save file the player picks in the browser count as build text supplied by the player?
options: yes for both: one-line amendment of decision 0004 item 4 and the CLAUDE.md Stack sentence
yes for the hotkey press only
no: paste box only
open_decisions.recommendation: Yes for both. Each load is the player's own act, the bytes are the same as a paste, the clipboard rule (one read per manual AshLight hotkey press) is kept, and the file pick follows decision 0033 (the core gets bytes, never a path). It removes most of the paste pain inside the floor.

open_decisions.question: Once the repository is public, may the User-Agent contact of every install, of the CI watcher and of the OAuth application be one project address (the repository's public issues page) so no player types a contact?
options: yes: project address by default, a typed per-install contact stays as an optional override
no: per-install contact only (decision 0015 as written)
open_decisions.recommendation: Yes. It is truthful and reachable, it serves the source's purpose (reach the tool's maintainers) better than a player's personal address, it keeps personal contacts out of tracked files, and it removes the only typed step between ticking 'Use web data' and seeing prices.

open_decisions.question: May the launcher (run.ps1, later the installed start) run the existing snapshot tool as its own hidden low-priority process when web data is on and the cache is missing or older than 24 h? Decision 0009 item 2 and the 0013 amendment tie the fetch to build time and build.ps1.
options: yes: amend 0009 item 2 to 'build time or start time, by the snapshot tool as its own process, never by the core'
no: build-time only (setup.ps1 runs the step when web data is already on)
open_decisions.recommendation: Yes. A player of an installed copy has no build step, so 'users miss the data and the switch' (the amendment's own Reverses-if) holds by construction; the fetch keeps the same opt-in, sources, User-Agent and contact, and the core still never fetches.

open_decisions.question: Before the flip: does the operator send one message to poe.ninja asking whether per-install polling at the tiered cadence is acceptable or a project mirror is wanted?
options: send the message
explicit skip: ship the tiered cadence without asking
open_decisions.recommendation: Send it. poe.ninja asks desktop apps to proxy through their own backend, and a public release multiplies requests by the install count; one message costs a minute and an objection after release costs the price feature. The tiered cadence (552 down to 200 overview GETs a day) ships either way.

rulings.question: May AshLight read files Path of Building writes on the player's disk: the builds folder (opt-in, path shown, newest fitting file per loop tick) or PoB's local API answer file? rulings.why: The hotkey load is the player's own act and the clipboard rule (one read per manual press) is kept. The file pick follows decision 0033 in shape (bytes, never a path), but the floor's read list does not name a picked file and no adjudicator or settled decision may widen it.

rulings.question: Before the flip: does the operator send one message to poe.ninja asking whether per-install polling at the tiered cadence is acceptable or a project mirror is wanted?

rulings.question: Updates: (a) may the core read the project's GitHub releases once a day while web data is on (wording of decision 0018 item 6)? (b) is a verified, staged update applied by itself at the next start after a 24 h hold (Settings switch to click-only), or only on a click?

(b) Verified update staged, applied automatically at next start after a 24 h hold; Settings switch gives click-only; previous version kept. The opt-in sentence must name the update check and the automatic apply; an opt-in given before that wording stays click-only (no check, no apply) until the player has seen it once.
rulings.alternatives: (a) yes, (b) click only (more upkeep for players); (a) no, notice from release page only (not glanceable).
rulings.why: Mirrors the settled TC-DRIFT daily read and 0013 single opt-in, so nothing hits the network while off. Auto-apply follows the minimal-interaction order; hash/attestation checks, hold and rollback bound the risk. GitHub API is a documented public endpoint, not a game endpoint.
rulings.reverses_if: GitHub or GGG terms bar the daily read, a bad release auto-applies in practice, or the operator wants click-only default.
rulings.record: amend decision 0013 (and 0018 item 6 wording) with the release-check and staged-apply clause

rulings.question: Go-public: the operator's go for step 1 (create the private repository and push main) and for step 4 (flip to public); and immutable releases on before the first v* tag?

rulings.question: Only if the needle scan finds the reviewed third-party set's names in history: publish with the affected history rewritten (needs an ORDER from the fleet owner) or from a fresh root commit?

rulings.question: Local stores derived from item text: (a) the worn-gear baseline as parsed stats in a bounded per-character file, on by default? (b) persist the BUILD-LIVE upgrade list across a restart?
rulings.ruling: (a) yes: worn-gear baseline as parsed mod lines in a bounded per-character file, on by default; (b) the BUILD-LIVE upgrade list stays memory-only.
rulings.alternatives: Baseline off by default; baseline memory-only; persist both (reverses 0045 with no trigger met).
rulings.why: Without (a) the baseline dies at every restart and breaks zero-click upgrade scoring. Parsed stats are not raw item text, so 0045's memory-only rule for the checked list is untouched. Local, bounded, under ops/runtime, no new read source, so the floor is not touched.
rulings.reverses_if: The operator rules local item-derived files unwanted, or a stored baseline is shown to leak names or paths. (b) reverses only on a 0045 Reverses-if.
rulings.record: new decision (beside 0045; cites 0036 for bounds and Clear run history)

rulings.question: May an off-by-default dev switch save the sanitized item text of a press as a fixture candidate in the sidecar (bounded, never tracked before review)? It answers the open facts about merchant-sale lines and note prices on copied items.

rulings.reverses_if: The operator rules item text must not be written even on the dev host, or a sample is found to hold unmasked names or account data.
